fact: UNCTAD's paper (September 2021) says the national ICT Policy and Strategy was developed in 2016 (FDRE 2016), is being implemented through listed interventions, and that its implementation is fragmented across projects and sectors.

The paper says that under the Communication Services Proclamation of 2019 the Ministry of Innovation and Technology is mandated to develop policy instruments, design programmes, mobilise resources and guide and monitor the telecom sector, with the Ethiopian Communications Authority regulating it.
IST-Africa's profile says Ethiopia's ICT policy, first drafted and submitted to the Council of Ministers in 2002, was revised and endorsed by the Council of Ministers in 2017.
IST-Africa's profile says the ICT policy was revised in 2017 with financial support from the World Bank; it states no domestic budget line.

IST-Africa's profile says the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology was established by Proclamation 691 in October 2010 for policy planning, development and implementation of ICT, and was merged with the Ministry of Science and Technology into the Ministry of Innovation and Technology in October 2018.

IST-Africa's profile says the National ICT Policy and Strategy 2009 set five objectives, among them accessible ICT infrastructure, skilled human resources, a legal framework, e-government and private-sector development.
